crossing_on_horseback.text: You ride across the valley at full speed. Behind you, Regalus—the bandit leader, the criminal who almost took your life and your medallion, the only remnant of your forgotten past—keeps snoring peacefully despite the jolts of the road. After several hours on horseback, you finally reach Kelia's Crossing, a small elven town ringed by immense fortifications, almost cut off from the rest of the world.

elf_and_eden_talk.text:
"Halt!" one of the elven legionaries at the gate barks. "No one enters the city without a pass; orders from the Dumvir." Eden flashes a mocking smile and simply nods toward the criminal tied to the back of his horse.

"Regalus!" the legionary exclaims. "Enter, the Dumvir will want to reward you personally. But know this: all entries and exits are forbidden from dusk onward." You follow Eden inside. The heavy city gates close behind you with a dull thud.

walking_city.text:
The streets are overflowing with people. You cut on foot through the central square, monopolized today by a gigantic market. Merchants and locals crowd the stalls, haggling loudly over all manner of goods. The sheer mass of bodies and voices creates a deafening, chaotic cacophony.

Inside the Curia, the political heart of the city, a scribe announces your arrival. The Dumvir, bent over his work, stops when he sees Regalus. The criminal, now awake, growls and struggles against his gag.

"That scoundrel Regalus, finally apprehended!" the Dumvir rejoices. With a snap of his fingers, he has a hefty purse dropped into Eden's hand. "To whom do I have the honor of paying this bounty?" The hunter introduces himself with his usual nonchalance, then turns toward you.

introduction_answer.text:
"A pleasure to meet you!" the politician replies, gripping your hand firmly. He signals two legionaries to escort Regalus to his cell, then immediately stops them.

"A criminal like Regalus implies a long, tedious trial," he sighs, pinching the bridge of his nose. "I do not have time for that, especially right now..."

He turns toward Eden. "Tell me, bounty hunter: by law, you are entitled to end his life. It would spare me a useless trial..." Eden strokes his beard, smelling an opportunity.

"Double the bounty and you've got a deal," he says.

"I'm afraid that's not in the budget," the Dumvir answers, his gaze shifting to you. "And your colleague? Would they be willing to rid Li'ark of a harmful criminal like Regalus?"

Refuse.

After a long, agonizing minute, his body goes rigid. The Dumvir watches in silence, then gives you a solemn nod of approval, clearly relieved and grateful that someone else has taken this burden upon themselves. His men quickly drag the corpse away.

discussing_undead.text:
In the privacy of his office, the Dumvir begins his tale. "An ancient and occult evil has been plaguing our region for weeks now... The undead," he explains. "Every night, these monsters crawl out from the bowels of the Globe and throw themselves against our walls. Piercing their rotten flesh with arrows is a pointless endeavor—they multiply and return in even greater numbers.

They massacred a little girl less than a week ago. The entire city was in uproar. I had no choice but to close the city gates and restrict all travel. We pray every day that our fortifications will hold for one more night." The Dumvir gazes out the window at the bustling market below before continuing.

dumvir_talks_necromancer.text:
"One of my scouts gave his life for the information I am about to share," the Dumvir says. He unrolls a map across his desk and drives the tip of his blade into a precise spot.

"We believe the surge of undead originates here, in the Crypt of the Ancients. Some ancient, forbidden magic is at work, and a necromancer of the worst kind must be behind it. I have sent my legionaries to assault the crypt time and again, but the coward hides behind an army of corpses."

"And what does the Empire think of all this?" Eden asks, intrigued.

The Dumvir scoffs. "The Empire is far too busy waging war against the Orcs in the south. They have no time for a small city like ours. No, hunters: find a way to slip inside the crypt, stop the necromancer, and I will make you rich. Ten thousand gold pieces—each. Will you answer the call?" His final question is aimed especially at you.

explanation_attempt.text:
You open your mouth, ready to correct the misunderstanding, but a hand lands on your shoulder: Eden's. He cuts you off.

"Twenty thousand each," the hunter says coldly. "We are talking about undead, black magic, necromancers—not common roadside bandits. No, twenty thousand is the minimum for a job that might cost me my life... and my partner's." His hand remains firmly on your shoulder.

The Dumvir stiffens. He hesitates for a long moment, staring into space.

"Deal," he finally says. Eden claps his hands, satisfied.

"Perfect! You will not be disappointed by our services, illustrious Dumvir. The next time we meet will be to celebrate a necromancer's death. Our regards!" The hunter pulls you outside, then turns to you. "Before you say anything, I'm pretty sure I promised you a drink, didn't I? Off to the tavern."
